title: Assessment grades are visible, but the course total is missing
symptom: Faculty can see an overall total, while learners see individual assessment marks but no final grade.
check: In Grades → Settings → Calculation Options, identify whether Calculated or Adjusted Final Grade is selected for release.
In Enter Grades, inspect the selected final column for the affected learner: distinguish an existing unreleased value from an empty value.
Open the final column’s menu → Enter Grades and inspect Released. Identify whether the intended scope is one learner or the whole class.
distinction: Calculating a total, publishing assessment feedback, displaying the calculation breakdown, and releasing the final grade are separate operations.
verify: After the authorized release, confirm the selected value in an approved learner view. The local release-final tour rehearses this distinction with synthetic records.

title: The final percentage does not match the syllabus
symptom: The entered assessment scores appear correct, but the faculty member’s manual total differs from Brightspace.
check: Compare the syllabus calculation with Grades → Settings → Calculation Options: Points, Weighted, or Formula.
In Manage Grades, separate top-level course weights from item weights inside each category; inspect category placement and maximum points.
Recalculate one anonymized example independently, including blanks and exemptions, before changing the structure.
distinction: A 50% item inside a category worth 40% contributes 20% of the course. Maximum points determine contribution in Points, but explicit weights determine it in Weighted.
verify: Explain the difference numerically. The sample’s scores produce 82% in Weighted and 86.67% in Points; matching one is meaningful only after confirming the intended policy.

title: A running grade suddenly fell, or missing work is being ignored
symptom: Learners report a much lower total after a setting change, or a higher total despite missing required work.
check: Inspect the actual affected cells: blank, recorded 0, and Exempt have different meanings.
Review Grades → Settings → Calculation Options → Grade Calculations; compare Exclude ungraded items with Treat ungraded items as 0.
Separate future/ungraded assessments from overdue required work, then check whether automatic overdue zeros are enabled and supported.
distinction: The blank-handling policy changes the calculation. Automatic zero grading records zeros for supported overdue work; a manually recorded zero remains included under either blank policy.
verify: With the sample’s Quiz 2 blank, the two policies produce 86% and 70%. Validate the real result against the intended missing-work policy, not the higher-looking total.

title: An assessment is out of the wrong number of points
symptom: An educator intended a 50-point assessment, but the grade column is out of 100 and the percentage looks wrong.
check: Identify the exact grade item and any associated activity; similarly named columns may not be the same assessment.
Compare the item’s Maximum Points with the intended assessment scale and inspect one learner’s existing earned score.
Determine whether the maximum was configured incorrectly or scores were entered on a different scale; assess the effect on other learners before proposing a correction.
distinction: Changing a maximum changes the denominator for the whole item. Changing an earned score changes one learner’s result; neither automatically expresses the educator’s intended rescaling.
verify: After a scoped correction, verify both the earned/possible display and one independently calculated percentage. The captured numeric-item form shows fields, not verified rescaling behavior.

title: The instructor changed a final grade, but the learner sees another value
symptom: The educator entered an adjusted result, but learners still see the calculated result or an older adjusted value.
check: Compare the Calculated and Adjusted Final Grade values for the same learner in Enter Grades.
Check Final Grade Released in Calculation Options and the learner’s release flag.
Establish whether an adjusted value was transferred before later assessment changes; it requires separate maintenance.
distinction: Adjusted is an independently maintained final value. Recalculating assessment totals does not automatically update that manual value, and only the selected final type is released.
verify: Confirm the intended final type, its exact value, and learner visibility together. Do not alter assessment scores merely to make the calculated column imitate an intentional adjustment.

title: Extra credit appears in its column but does not increase the total as expected
symptom: Bonus credit is recorded, but the category or final total stops increasing or is capped at 100%.
check: Establish whether this is a bonus item or an above-maximum score on an ordinary item.
Inspect the item’s Bonus and Can Exceed settings, then the containing category’s cap and the final grade’s cap.
For Weighted, trace the bonus weight through its category weight; an uncategorized bonus uses its own course-level weight.
distinction: Bonus adds earned credit without expanding the normal denominator. Can Exceed controls a cap; enabling it only on the item does not remove category or final caps.
verify: Work through one numerical example at each level. Confirm that the resulting total follows the approved extra-credit policy. There is no dedicated working tour for this case.

title: Dropping the lowest quiz does not produce the expected result
symptom: The educator expects the lowest quiz to be ignored, but the category total or an interim calculation disagrees.
check: Confirm all intended quizzes belong to the same category and inspect its distribution and drop count.
Check eligible non-bonus items, maximum points, weights, exemptions, and remaining items; exemptions are removed before the drop rule.
Identify whether the disputed value is Final Calculated Grade or a separate interim Calculated item, whose handling can depend on administrator configuration.
distinction: Category dropping is not the same as excluding an assessment for everyone or exempting one learner. Different calculation contexts may not use the same drop behavior.
verify: Reproduce the selected dropped item and the remaining denominator for one learner. Keep partial or unequal-item examples outside the simulator’s documented subset.

title: A grade column was deleted during cleanup
symptom: A faculty member removed a column or category and now cannot find the expected grade structure.
check: Determine whether a category, an individual item, or a larger gradebook operation was removed; deleting a category leaves its items standalone.
Inspect Grades → Manage Grades → More Actions → View Event Log for the affected item and an available Restore action.
Check item type and Manage Grades permission; Formula and Calculated grade items are excluded from the documented restoration option.
distinction: There is a documented restore route for eligible deleted items. “No undo exists” is not a correct general answer, and an empty category is not the same as its contained score columns.
verify: Verify the recovered item, relevant learner scores, and resulting calculation. The menu was captured; the local restoration form is a teaching model rather than a captured restoration test.

title: The percentage and letter or 4.0 grade appear inconsistent
symptom: A displayed percentage seems to qualify for one grade label, but the learner receives a different symbol.
check: Inspect the applicable scheme under Grades → Schemes and compare its Start % boundaries with the approved grading scale.
Check whether the individual item or final grade uses a different scheme from the course default.
Distinguish the stored percentage from displayed decimals; for Selectbox items, also inspect the scheme’s Assigned Value %.
distinction: Numeric items use scheme ranges to display achievement. Selectbox choices can supply an assigned numeric percentage, so schemes are not universally display-only.
verify: Check a value immediately below and above the disputed threshold against the intended scale. Do not introduce a rounding policy simply to make the label match a rounded display.

title: An assignment created a duplicate grade column or writes to the wrong one
symptom: Faculty see two similarly named columns, or an assignment result appears in an unexpected grade item.
check: In Manage Grades, compare the columns and their Association rather than relying on names alone.
In the assignment editor, inspect In Grade Book → Edit or Link to Existing and identify the linked numeric item.
Compare maximum points and existing scores before deciding which association or duplicate needs correction.
distinction: The assignment activity and its grade item are separate objects connected by an association. Renaming either does not prove they are linked correctly.
verify: Verify the chosen association and a published evaluation’s destination without deleting existing scored columns as a shortcut. This simulator stores links but does not reproduce grading synchronization.

title: The assignment has been marked, but learners cannot see the feedback
symptom: The evaluator sees a score and comments, while the learner sees no assignment result.
check: Open the affected learner’s evaluation and inspect whether the work is saved as draft or published.
Confirm the result is for the correct learner and submission, then inspect the associated grade item’s visibility separately.
Establish whether publication is intended for this learner now or for the class together before choosing the publication scope.
distinction: Saving evaluation work and publishing it are different states. Releasing the course final grade does not publish an assignment’s draft feedback.
verify: Confirm the published score and feedback in the learner’s assignment view and, where associated, the correct grade column. Evaluation and publication are documentation-only here.

title: The assignment accepts work after the deadline, or closes too early
symptom: The assignment remains submittable after its due date, or learners lose submission access earlier than intended.
check: Compare Due Date with Start Date and End Date under Availability Dates & Conditions.
Inspect visibility and the access/submission restriction chosen for each availability boundary.
Check any special-access dates for the affected learner.
distinction: The due date marks a deadline; availability boundaries and their selected restrictions determine access or submission behavior.
verify: Check the intended learner’s actual submission availability. The working tour demonstrates the simplified overdue-but-open case without uploading files.

title: One learner needs an assignment extension
symptom: Faculty need different submission dates for one learner while retaining the normal class schedule.
check: Confirm the normal due/end dates and the requested individual extension.
Open Availability Dates & Conditions → Manage Special Access and inspect its access mode.
Review that learner’s selected dates and ensure the end date permits the intended submission period.
distinction: An individual exception differs from changing the assignment’s normal dates. The option restricting access to only selected users has a different purpose.
verify: Verify the exception for the learner and the unchanged class schedule. The special-access controls were captured; this case has no dedicated working tour.

title: One learner needs extra time on one quiz
symptom: The requested timing change applies to a particular quiz rather than every quiz in the course.
check: Confirm the quiz, base time limit, affected learner, requested total duration, and whether an attempt has already started.
Inspect the quiz’s Availability Dates & Conditions → Manage Special Access and its individual time override.
Check Classlist accommodations as well, so the saved quiz exception does not produce an unintended duration.
distinction: Quiz Special Access is assessment-specific; Classlist accommodations apply across the course. A New Time Limit is a total minute value, not an extra-minute increment.
verify: The practice case keeps the standard limit at 30 and gives the chosen learner 45. Verify a real learner through an approved method; Quiz Preview is insufficient for individual timing.

title: The learner needs a timing allowance across all course quizzes
symptom: An approved requirement calls for the same timing rule throughout this course.
check: Establish whether the requirement is a multiplier or a fixed number of extra minutes; these differ on quizzes of different lengths.
Inspect Classlist → learner menu → Edit Accommodations → Quizzes → Timing.
Review existing quiz-specific exceptions before assuming every quiz is using the course allowance.
distinction: A 1.5 multiplier gives 45/90 minutes on 30/60-minute quizzes; a fixed extra 15 gives 45/75. The accommodation belongs to this course.
verify: Verify the effective duration and which setting supplied it. The local tour clears an old quiz override and demonstrates 30 + 15 = 45 minutes.

title: The quiz is visible, but the learner cannot start another attempt
symptom: The learner can find the quiz but has no usable Start Quiz option.
check: Check the learner’s allowed, completed, and in-progress attempts before adding another attempt or resetting anything.
Compare current availability and special-access dates with the time of the reported failure.
Inspect password requirements and any retake-incorrect-questions rule; pending evaluation or no incorrect questions can affect a retake.
distinction: Quiz visibility does not establish eligibility to begin an attempt. An attempt problem is different from hidden content.
verify: Confirm the permitted attempt becomes available without discarding existing attempt evidence. Attempt delivery, passwords, and retake behavior are not modeled in the local app.

title: A completed quiz has a score, but the gradebook is blank
symptom: The instructor sees a quiz attempt score while the expected Grades column contains no result.
check: Identify the linked numeric grade item and check that the learner’s attempt was submitted and evaluated.
Inspect the attempt’s publication state and the quiz’s Evaluation & Feedback options for publishing and updating the gradebook.
Check the gradebook column and learner visibility separately from the attempt-results display.
distinction: Attempt evaluation, publication, gradebook synchronization, and the learner’s results display are related but distinct. A visible attempt score does not prove all four occurred.
verify: Verify the published result reaches the intended grade item and is visible where requested. The capture shows configuration controls; synchronization needs checking in real Brightspace.

title: Learners cannot find a module that staff can see
symptom: The course opens, but a week or module is absent for learners.
check: Confirm course access before narrowing the issue to a particular module or topic.
Inspect the affected module’s visibility and availability dates, then check the intended topic separately.
If the problem is learner-specific, inspect applicable release conditions and enrollment rather than changing shared visibility immediately.
distinction: Course access, module visibility, topic visibility, and conditional release are different layers. Seeing content as staff is not a learner-access test.
verify: The working tour reveals the sample Week 1 module and checks the local learner view. Real topics and release conditions require a separate approved learner check.

title: Copied course content contains broken or unavailable links
symptom: A copied page opens, but its document, activity link, or embedded resource fails.
check: Record the exact error and identify whether the failing link is the topic itself or a link inside its body.
Locate the intended destination in the new course and inspect availability; an Unavailable Quicklink can indicate dates rather than a broken link.
Compare the destination URL with the intended course/resource. Use the current Content experience’s Edit link or editor Quicklink controls to repair a confirmed wrong destination.
distinction: A copied page is not proof that every referenced destination was copied or is available. Do not replace links blindly when access dates explain the error.
verify: Open the repaired resource through the original learner-facing page and verify the correct destination. Course copying and link repair are documentation-only in this app.

title: The Content screen does not match the faculty help guide
symptom: An educator cannot find controls shown in instructions written for another Content layout.
check: Identify whether the course uses Classic Content or New Content Experience before supplying navigation steps.
Compare the specific missing control with the relevant experience; do not treat every layout difference as a permission failure.
If an experience change is requested, establish whether the institution enables it and permits that role to switch the course.
distinction: The Content experience changes navigation and presentation for the course, including learners; it is not just a personal cosmetic preference.
verify: The working tour demonstrates capability versus course choice using a simplified configuration model. Confirm the actual institutional switching controls before recommending a real change.

title: One learner cannot access content despite its visible status
symptom: Shared visibility is enabled, but access differs between learners.
check: Inspect the release conditions attached to the affected content or activity and identify the exact required event or grade.
Check the affected learner’s recorded completion/score for the referenced object, including whether the reference points to the intended activity.
If the learner is exempt, verify how that exemption interacts with the particular condition rather than assuming it supplies a qualifying grade.
distinction: Visible status does not establish that a learner has satisfied a release condition. An exemption removes grading responsibility; it does not automatically supply prerequisite achievement.
verify: Confirm the required condition and permitted access using an appropriate learner account. The local app does not implement a release-condition engine.

title: A person can sign in but is missing from this course
symptom: A staff member or learner has a working account but does not appear in the expected course roster.
check: Confirm the correct course offering and existing account identity; check Classlist filters before concluding membership is absent.
Inspect the course enrollment and assigned role; an account existing elsewhere does not establish membership here.
Determine whether enrollment is managed manually or by an institutional system, and check your permission to enroll into the requested role.
distinction: Account creation and course enrollment solve different problems. Duplicating an existing account can leave the original access problem unresolved.
verify: Verify the expected person and role in Classlist, then actual course access. The local account/enrollment tour uses fictional data and does not reproduce roster synchronization.

title: A staff member can enter the course but cannot edit
symptom: The person can view course material but lacks the specific editing action faculty expect.
check: Identify the exact blocked action and the person’s role in this course; compare with a correctly authorized colleague.
Separate changing one course enrollment from changing the permissions of the role definition.
Ask the administrator to inspect the relevant role scope, dependencies, and interactions when the course enrollment alone does not explain access.
distinction: Changing a role definition can affect everyone using it; assigning a different role to one enrollment has a narrower scope.
verify: Confirm the intended action works for the affected person without granting unrelated capabilities. The working role tour exposes only five local practice permissions, not the institutional permission matrix.

title: The course is active, but learners still cannot open it
symptom: Faculty can enter the course, but enrolled learners report it is unavailable or cannot be opened.
check: Inspect Course Admin → Course Offering Information → Course is active.
Compare course Start Date and End Date with the intended access window; an active course can still be outside that window.
Confirm the affected learner’s enrollment and account status; if the active checkbox is unavailable, establish the required permission with the administrator.
distinction: Active status and course availability dates both matter. Faculty access is not evidence that learners can enter.
verify: Confirm an approved learner can enter during the intended period. The content-access tour models status and dates locally; it does not recreate every staff access exception.

title: Copied assessments still use last term’s dates
symptom: A copied course has the right activities but outdated due and availability dates.
check: In Course Admin → Manage Dates, filter and inspect the affected objects and the date fields that need changing.
Choose between setting selected dates with Bulk Edit Dates and shifting a schedule with Bulk Offset Dates.
Review the intended interval and selected objects before saving, then inspect exceptions whose dates should not move uniformly.
distinction: Setting every selected deadline to one date differs from offsetting a schedule. Updating due dates alone may leave old start/end restrictions.
verify: Check representative activities near the beginning and end of the term and confirm their learner availability. Manage Dates was captured, but bulk date changes are reference-only here.
